text:
maya: Heads-up — I'm opening a docs PR to migrate the tenant-specific autoscale examples to the new unified ScalePolicy model. Goal: one canonical JSON example, add per-tenant cooldown notes, call out preemption behavior for Dedicated, and include a tiny Go SDK snippet. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/789 :paperclip:

alex: Thanks — can you also add a short FAQ blurb about what happens when burst capacity hits a reserved pool? PMs keep asking if we should recommend burst_policy or reserved_pool for spikes.

maya: @alex yes — planning to add a short recommendation table: reserved_pool for predictable bursts; burst_policy for infrequent spikes. Will add sample metrics to justify.

samir: One request: the old examples used YAML and referenced "tenant_label" a lot. For the new unified model we should remove tenant-specific keys and show how to use "tenant_selector" field instead. Also add a migration snippet for Terragrunt users.

maya: Good call. I'll replace YAML with JSON and include a tiny terragrunt/terraform snippet.

ryan: For SLA wording, legal wants a line about "best-effort preemption" vs "scheduled preemption" — can we include an example of fallback ordering (canary -> standard -> fallback-model)?

lin: Also add an explicit example for isolation: show annotation "isolation: hardened" and how that maps to reserved pools and eviction policies. Ops will love a one-liner for runbooks.

maya: Draft JSON example I'm planning to include (short):
```json
{
  "scalePolicy": {
    "minReplicas": 1,
    "maxReplicas": 20,
    "cooldownSeconds": 120,
    "burstPolicy": "best_effort",
    "tenantSelector": {"matchLabels": {"app": "payments"}},
    "isolation": "hardened"
  }
}
```

maya: Tiny Go SDK snippet I'm adding for the "apply policy" section:```go
client := redwood.NewClient("$REDWOOD_KEY")
pol := redwood.ScalePolicy{Min:1, Max:20, Cooldown:120}
if err := client.ApplyScalePolicy(ctx, "tenant-payments", pol); err != nil {
  log.Fatal(err)
}
```

samir: Can we also include the CLI equivalent? e.g. `redwoodctl scale set --tenant payments --min 1 --max 20 --cooldown 120` — ops uses that a lot.

maya: Yup, adding CLI snippet. Also will add a short note: "If preemption occurs, requests are routed to fallback-model according to the rollout policy; see rollout examples."

alex: Reviewer volunteers: I can review the migration instructions. @ryan can you do SLA wording review? @lin can you sanity-check isolation mapping and ops notes?

ryan: I'll review SLA phrasing tomorrow morning.

lin: On it — I'll verify mapping to reserved pools/eviction in the runbook.

docs-bot: PR opened by maya: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/789 — labels: docs, dedicated, scalepolicy

maya: One open question for the thread: should the docs recommend default cooldownSeconds = 60 or 120? Perf team suggests 120 for noisy workloads. We might call out a per-workload tuning table.

samir: 120 seems safer as a default; add a short table with recommendations: low-latency chat=60, webhooks/batch=120+, background jobs=300.

alex: Agree. Also add link to the perf benchmark that supports the numbers (internal link).

maya: Will do. I'll push the PR with the JSON examples + Go + CLI + Terragrunt snippet and tag reviewers. Expect small follow-ups for wording. :rocket:

ryan: Thanks — will review SLA section after lunch.

lin: LGTM for ops structure, will check examples once the PR is up.

maya: PR updated: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/789/files — ping reviewers.

docs-bot: maya merged pull request 789 into main — closed by maya.

alex: Thanks! Quick post-merge ask: can we backport the migration note to the 1.2 handbook anchor? Not urgent but helpful for oncalls.

maya: Noted — opening backport PR.

samir: Awesome work, thanks everyone.
